newsitem.title: FINLAND: Huhtamaki makes first acquisition as profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Huhtamaki makes first acquisition as profits rise.

text.p: Finnish confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki Oy on Tuesday reported a sharp improvement in profits and announced its first step on an expected acquisitive path.

Huhtamaki said it would buy privately-owned Pacific World Packaging (PWP), a leading cup and container maker for the food and food services industries in the Asia-Pacific region with annual net sales of 350 million markka ($71.1 million).
The group had been expected to seek growth in its remaining units through acquisitions after it last year sold its pharmaceuticals division Leiras to German Schering AG.
The announced purchase of PWP came alongside a 33 percent increase in Huhtamaki's 1996 profits and the group forecast further improvement this year.

Huhtamaki's 1996 profit after financial items was 416 million markka ($84.5 million) -- up from 312 million in 1995 -- with about equal contributions from the confectionery unit Leiras and packaging unit Polarcup.
Net sales fell to 7.51 billion markka from 7.84 billion.
Earnings per share rose to 10.29 markka from 7.56 markka in 1995 and this year would bring a further increase in profits but these would be generated later in the year than before, it said.

"After a slow start of the year, a further improvement in earnings per share is expected for 1997," Huhtamaki said in a statement. "Strong seasonal sales in the second half of 1997 will contribute to another full-year profit improvement."
Operating earnings in the first third of the year would represent only of a fifth of the annual total, it added.

The acquisition PWP would give Polarcup a total of six manufacturing units in Australia, two in China and one in Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia and New Zealand, making the Polarcup division an industry leader in the Asia-Pacific region, it said.
Huhtamaki warned analysts and investors that acquisitions would make it difficult to forecast its net sales development, but the European market would be on a steady trend.

"Huhtamaki's main Western European markets are likely to develop steadily," it said. "Further growth is sought from expanding product segments and the new markets of Eastern Europe and Asia." ($ = 4.921 Finnish Markka)
